_comment: Route list for the NEW UI's hash routes (feat/ui-next, ui/src/next). Built 2026-09-10 against router.ts (SUBS table), hubs/index.ts (HUB_ORDER/HUB_META/SHEETS registry) and every hub's sheets/index.ts + reg-*.ts fragments, cross-checked against `data-testid` attributes actually present in ui/src/next/hubs/** and ui/src/next/shell/**. Extended by T-R7-21 with the marker families the wave-2 tasks reported (video, video library, temperature compensation, slew rate, the ephemeris card, the satellites-and-comets card) and with a `_pending` entry for every family whose markers need rig state the sim does not produce. Each `_pending` says WHICH state and names the family it stands for, so a later harness that can seed the state knows what to turn on; each live entry carries a `_note` naming the family it anchors. Every entry asserts ONE testid, which is why a marker that only renders at some widths is pending rather than asserted (probe.py walks every width with the same route).
_testid_vs_marker: Every route asserts a `data-testid` (added to probe.py this run -- see README). A few also carry a text `marker` as a second, independent check where the visible label is unambiguous and cheap to also assert (mirrors routes_classic.json's belt-and-braces style); most do not, because testid alone is the harness's real gate here and doubling every route up with a text marker just re-derives the same testid map from prose.
_param_correction: `#/session/files` reads `params.src`, NOT `params.source` (ui/src/next/hubs/session/sheets/files.tsx:177) -- and the value the UI itself uses for 'tonight' is `src=current` (files.tsx:511, the TONIGHT chip), not `src=tonight`. Used the real names, per the brief's own instruction to use what the code carries.
_classic_marker: The classic header's STATUS strip (`ui/src/App.tsx:599`) is `hidden md:flex` -- invisible at 390px, so it would false-FAIL the probe's visible-only text match on a phone width for no reason related to whether classic actually mounted. 'Equipment' (the default view's own nav label, App.tsx NAV / BottomNav) is visible at every width and is safe here specifically because the #/classic route never clicks anywhere -- it only has to prove the legacy root mounted with its default view, not that a click landed on the right screen, so the nav-label collision risk routes_classic.json's own notes warn about does not apply.
_pending_list: Six entries are `_pending` and skipped unless --include-pending (probe.py:468-472). Every one was MEASURED with --include-pending on 2026-09-10 rather than assumed, and the shots are in .probe/out-pending: session-plan-schedule (needs a loaded plan whose first target id is t1 AND a width >= 768); session-flows-canvas (passes at 820/1440, fails at 390 - the canvas is off-phone only and no one testid is valid at three widths); rig-capture-result (the promotable frame the SAVE TO GALLERY card offers exists only after a real shot, and it is not on the status bus); weather-dew-loop (status.dew is null on the sim); session-now-ledger (status.channels is null until a live stack has frames); sky-passes (needs downloaded TLE elements and a satellite picked); settings-optics-migration (needs a browser holding the legacy optics key, or an engine with no optics.aperture_mm - the two halves of that family need opposite worlds). rig-camera-dew and sky-targets-ephemeris were promoted to live on one run's evidence and put back after the next run failed them - the first because the sim publishes a dew loop inconsistently, the second because the targets sheet can spend longer ranking the catalog than probe.py waits for a marker. rig-power-port went the other way and stayed live: the sim rig does bring up a six-port PowerBox, so the per-port rows are real.
_role_note: Under --auth --role viewer the four WEATHER routes (weather, weather-sky, weather-sky-overlay, weather-radar) fail by design, not by defect: a viewer has no view.weather, so WeatherHub.tsx:94 renders the honest `wx-no-cap` card ("WEATHER IS NOT VISIBLE TO THIS ROLE") in place of the screen, and probe.py has one testid per route for every role. A viewer walk should read those four as PASS-with-wx-no-cap. Everything else in this list renders for a viewer with its controls honest-locked rather than hidden, which is the point.

routes.name: sky
routes._note: The Sky hub's DEFAULT screen, which is ATLAS mode on every device now (ui/src/next/hubs/sky/finder/prefs.ts DEFAULT_MODE): #/sky with nothing stored renders the pannable survey canvas populated by tonight's ranked targets, not the schematic finder. hub-sky stays the marker on purpose - it is the hub root and renders in every mode, so this route keeps passing whichever mode a phone has chosen, and sky-targets-on-atlas below is what asserts the default specifically. Family on the default screen: hub-sky, sky-suggested, sky-atlas, atlas-canvas, atlas-search, atlas-markers, atlas-reticle, atlas-aim, atlas-layers, sky-cta, sky-dome-card.
routes._expected_errors_why: MEASURED on the sim rig: it has no offline sky pack and config.survey.online_fetch is off by default, so every HiPS tile the WebGL engine asks for 404s - 11 to 16 of them per load, which is the exact state the atlas-degraded banner exists to explain, not a defect the probe should hide behind a red route. The URL entry is precise; the console entry has to be the 404 TEXT because a console message carries no URL, and it only suppresses the browser echo - a 404 on any other endpoint still fails this route through the failed-REQUEST check, which matches on the URL.

routes._note: The skydome card, at the bottom of the same default ATLAS screen - it answers about the whole sky rather than the reticle, so it is on every mode.

routes.name: sky-atlas

SkyHub consumes and drops the parameter on arrival, exactly as it does ?lock= and ?frame=1, so the address bar reads #/sky again by the time the screenshot is taken - that is the feature, not a miss. Family: sky-atlas, atlas-canvas, atlas-search, atlas-degraded, atlas-lock-in-finder, atlas-frame, sky-atlas-mode.

On the sim rig there is no survey pack and online fetch is off, so the canvas draws its dark radial-gradient placeholder and the atlas-degraded banner sits under it; both clear the probe 16x16 floor.

routes.name: sky-targets-on-atlas
routes._note: The finder's ranked targets drawn over the atlas as the design's label pills (name and altitude, the lock ring on the locked one), plus the reticle at the finder's aim. Asserted at #/sky rather than ?mode=atlas because this is what the DEFAULT screen has to carry. The overlay is sized from the measured canvas, so it clears the probe's 16x16 floor only once the canvas has laid out. Family: atlas-markers, atlas-reticle, atlas-aim, atlas-layers, atlas-survey-off.

routes.name: weather-dew-loop
routes._pending: the weather band's heater line reads the dew LOOP's own snapshot (status.dew, hub.py:6650), which the sim never publishes: the node appears only once a dew controller exists and has ticked, and GET /api/status on the probe server returns dew: null. The camera sheet's FOLLOW DEW switch is a different gate and does render - see rig-camera-dew. Family: wx-dew-loop plus the margin/power readouts that hang off the same node.

routes.name: session-now-ledger
routes._pending: the night ledger line reads status.channels[], which is null on the sim rig until a live stack has taken frames per filter. Family: channel-ledger-note, channel-missing-note (channel-tint-note was removed by T-U7b-2 and is named in no route).

routes.name: session-flows-canvas
routes._pending: MEASURED, not assumed: with --include-pending this route passes at 820 and 1440 and fails at 390, because FlowsScreen.tsx:310 renders the canvas host only off-phone and the same hash is the flow LIST on a phone. probe.py asserts one testid at every width, so a width-conditional marker cannot be expressed; the shot at 820/1440 is in .probe/out-pending. Family: session-flows-canvas, flows-canvas-back, flows-canvas-no-flow.

routes.name: rig-capture-video
routes._note: VIDEO is route state, not a tab: CaptureScreen.tsx:112 reads params.mode. The sim camera publishes video_path 'none' (test_status_bus_s7 pins it), so this shot is the honest no-route card, which is a screen with its own copy.

routes.name: rig-capture-video-refusal
routes._note: the honest refusal card the sim camera earns: video_path 'none' means cannotRecord, and VideoMode.tsx:257-262 renders the sentence plus 'single frames, LOOP and Live View still work'. video-no-route is the OTHER branch (a server with no video route at all) and does not render against this server, which has POST /api/capture/video. Family: video-refusal, video-server-refusal, video-no-route, video-roi, video-controls, video-fps, video-exposure, video-gain, video-duration, video-estimate, video-record, video-stop, video-recordings, video-all-recordings - the ROI and controls block is the not-cannotRecord branch and needs a camera with a burst path.

routes.name: rig-capture-result
routes._pending: the SAVE TO GALLERY / SAVE AS TARGET card renders only while the rig holds a promotable frame (hub.py's promotable buffer, filled by a single shot). The harness takes no exposure, and the buffer is not on the status bus, so there is nothing to arm it with. Family: result-save-gallery, result-save-as-target, result-promote-note, result-saved-path.

routes.name: sky-targets
routes._expected_errors_why: MEASURED on the sim rig: it has no offline sky pack and config.survey.online_fetch is off by default, so every HiPS tile the WebGL engine asks for 404s - and since ATLAS became the Sky hub's default mode every #/sky route mounts that engine, including the ones whose subject is a sheet on top of it. That is the exact state the atlas-degraded banner exists to explain, not a defect the probe should hide behind a red route. The URL entry is precise; the console entry has to be the 404 TEXT because a console message carries no URL, and it only suppresses the browser echo - a 404 on any other endpoint still fails this route through the failed-REQUEST check, which matches on the URL.

routes.name: sky-targets-ephemeris
routes._pending: MEASURED: the satellites-and-comets card sits UNDER the suggested-target list, and the sheet spends up to 15 s ranking the catalog before that list exists ('Ranking tonight... 9s' in .probe/out/1440/sky-targets-ephemeris.png). probe.py waits 8 s for a marker, so this route passes or times out depending on how fast the rig ranks - it passed at all three widths in one run and timed out at 1440 in the next. The card itself is real and carries the ephemeris note; it needs either a longer wait than the harness gives or a pre-ranked catalog. Family: targets-ephemeris, ephemeris-note, ephemeris-settings-link, target-row-satellite, target-row-comet, comet-pick, comet-geocentric.

routes.name: session-plan-schedule
routes._pending: needs a loaded plan whose first target id is t1, and a width >= 768; the harness seeds neither

routes.name: rig-camera-dew
routes._pending: MEASURED BOTH WAYS on 2026-09-10, which is why it is pending rather than live: the FOLLOW DEW switch and its line render only while the rig has a dew LOOP (camera.tsx:718, `dewLoop.kind !== "absent"`), and the sim publishes one inconsistently - one probe run found the switch at all three widths, the next found the honest no-loop wording instead (SENSOR WINDOW HEATER · 'set the power by hand', .probe/out/390/rig-camera-dew.png). A route that is a coin toss is worse than one that says why. Family: camera-follow-dew, dew-loop-line, dew-manual-note, dew-ramp, dew-margin-full, dew-margin-off, dew-min-power, dew-max-power, dew-override, dew-refusal.

routes.name: rig-mount-slew-rate
routes._note: the lifted slew-rate dial (D-RIG-4). Family: mount-slew-rate, mount-rate-note, mount-ra-step, mount-dec-step - all four render unconditionally in the sheet.

routes.name: rig-focuser-tempcomp
routes._note: the temperature-compensation card (D-RIG-2). It renders when the status bus carries focuser.temp_comp, which hub.py:6757-6771 publishes for any connected focuser (the sim's reads 'temperature compensation is off'). tempcomp-absent is the other branch and only appears on an engine older than S7.

routes.name: rig-power-port
routes._note: the sim rig DOES bring up a switch (Sim PowerBox UPBv2, six ports), so the per-port rows are real: id 0 is the Mount port. Family: port-settings-<id>, port-protect-<id>, port-follow-dew-<id> - the last two are inside the port's own settings sheet, one tap in from this row.

routes.name: rig-video-library
routes._note: GET /api/captures/video answers {recordings: []} on the sim, so this is the empty library with its KEEP % row - a real screen. Family: rig-video-library, video-library-body, video-library-total (total needs at least one recording).

routes.name: settings-optics-migration
routes._pending: the aperture/reducer migration note (T-U7b-9, D-SET-1) renders only for a browser that still holds the legacy `astrodeck-next-optics-aux` key AND a role that cannot write config.site_optics; the probe starts from a clean profile with no localStorage and signs in as admin. Its sibling `optics-aperture-unsupported` needs the opposite - an ENGINE with no optics.aperture_mm - and this server publishes the field (OpticsSheet.tsx:171), so neither branch is reachable here. Family: optics-legacy-note, optics-aperture-unsupported.

routes.name: settings-ephemeris
routes._note: the ephemeris card inside SKY DATA (the settings row renamed by the U7b ruling). Family: settings-ephemeris, ephemeris-row-satellites, ephemeris-row-comets, ephemeris-note-satellites, ephemeris-note-comets, ephemeris-refresh, ephemeris-message, ephemeris-error, ephemeris-lock; ephemeris-absent is the 404 branch and does not render against this server.

routes.name: root
routes._note: THE ROOT IS THE CLASSIC APP AGAIN (2026-09-15, ui/src/rootChoice.ts DEFAULT_ROOT = "classic"). This route used to assert a new-UI marker; it now asserts the same marker as the #/classic route above, because #/ and #/classic mount the same root. 'Equipment' is the classic default view's own nav label - see _classic_marker for why that string and not the header STATUS strip. Flip DEFAULT_ROOT to "next" and THIS is the route that must be changed back, together with next-home below.

routes.name: next-home
routes._note: The alias that always reaches the new UI's home whichever root is default (router.ts NEXT_ROOT_ALIAS / NEXT_HOME). AppRoot.resolveRoot canonicalises it onto #/sky on arrival, so the address bar reads #/sky by the time the screenshot is taken - the same consume-and-drop shape as ?mode=atlas above, and the reason the marker is the sky hub's and not an alias-specific one. This is the new UI's half of the two-way door; the classic half is the OPEN THE NEW SIX-HUB UI link in classic Settings (data-testid link-next-ui).
routes._expected_errors_why: Same measured sim-rig state as the other #/sky routes: no offline sky pack and config.survey.online_fetch off, so every HiPS tile 404s.
